newsitem.title: USA: NASD's Zarb to see LILCO-Brooklyn merger through.
newsitem.headline: NASD's Zarb to see LILCO-Brooklyn merger through.

text.p: Frank Zarb, newly-elected National Association of Securities Dealers chairman said Tuesday he will conclude outstanding issues overhanging the proposed merger between two utilities, despite his new role.

"We have a project underway that has a short fuse and that we're either going to have a solution put in place to the Long Island Power question over the next several months or we're not going to get it done," Zarb said in a teleconference call.
On December 29, 1996, Brooklyn Union Gas and Long Island Lighting Co agreed to merge in a stock deal that would create a $4 billion electric and natural gas company.
"I'm going to see that to a finish and I think we'll be successful over the near term," he said in his first interview as the new chairman and chief executive officer of the NASD.
Earlier today, NASD named Zarb, chairman of the Long Island Power Authority, to the top spot of the self-regulatory agency that runs the Nasdaq stock market.
He will assume his duties on February 24, succeeding Joseph Hardiman, who is retiring on January 31 after nearly 10 years of service to the NASD.
